assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is a minimal stochastic model for nonlinear growth, and it defines a universality class with non-Gaussian, random-matrix-type (Tracy-Widom) fluctuations. It connects interface growth, directed polymers, stochastic dynamics and integrable probability. It is original and conceptually clear, and it has shaped non-equilibrium statistical physics for decades. From my own field of stochastic processes and random matrices I rate it very highly.
assessment.attribution: Kardar and Zhang are the originators of the 1986 theory (the supplied credit lacks Parisi, who is not among the credited names). Takeuchi supplied the decisive experimental confirmation in turbulent liquid crystals, including universal distributions and the geometry-dependent statistics. A theory-plus-experiment trio is a fair configuration. The proper weight of Takeuchi relative to the mathematical-physics solutions of the exact KPZ distributions, which are not credited here, is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Almost four decades old, with strong independent confirmation from liquid-crystal experiments and several other systems, such as colloidal and other growth fronts, plus exact solutions. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, not premature.
uncertainties: Exact-solution contributors (e.g. mathematical physicists) are not in the credited names, so the intellectual credit is incomplete.
The breadth of experimental realisations beyond the one flagship experiment is only partly established, and I have not independently checked this.
Whether the committee considers the 2021 prize for complex systems to cover enough of the area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their 1995 proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the later proposals for quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions opened the field of controlled quantum many-body engineering. It is original, clear and has had lasting influence on both quantum information and many-body physics. I judge it among the most significant theory contributions of the last three decades.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the evident joint originators of the ion-trap gate proposal and share the central proposals for quantum simulation. The two-name configuration is natural and clean, and it avoids the allocation problems of the larger lists.
assessment.maturity: The ion-trap computing proposal was realised experimentally within a few years and has since been confirmed by many independent groups. The 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) recognised experiments on single quantum systems, and the 2025 prize recognised circuit macroscopic quantum effects, so this is a fairly timely complementary recognition.
uncertainties: Experimental ion-trap leaders such as Blatt or Wineland-type contributions could be argued to need joint recognition, which affects the allocation.
Overlap with other quantum-simulation candidates on this list, which share Zoller, complicates a single-candidate prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, gives stability and accuracy at the 10^-18 level. It enables tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear, specific invention with a lasting measurement impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Jun Ye led the highest-precision demonstrations and the strontium clocks that realised it. Both are central. Other groups, such as Lemonde, Hollberg, Lukin-Ye theory, and Ludlow, also contributed, but a pair is a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories worldwide and still improving. The 2005 prize covered the frequency comb, and the clock is the natural follow-on. Recognition would be timely, and the redefinition of the second may add further maturity.
uncertainties: Attribution to Ye versus other clock leaders (e.g. NIST and JILA colleagues) could be contested.
The measurement-science impact is partly prospective, since the redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, as far as I know.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a new classification of band structures by topology. It is conceptually deep and original, and it has stimulated an enormous subsequent literature in materials and quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the founding theoretical proposals, and Molenkamp led the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. The credited trio is plausible, but Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and Moore are not in the supplied names, so there is real allocation tension.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent experiments (ARPES, transport), and the interpretation is stable. The 2016 Nobel Prize (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz) recognised topological phase transitions and matter, so this is partly adjacent, and the question is whether the remaining step is distinct enough.
uncertainties: The credited list omits other decisive contributors, so a prize here would be disputed.
Possible overlap with the 2016 topology prize reduces novelty of the recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory established the physics of flocking: long-range order in two dimensions in a non-equilibrium system and the associated scaling laws. They are original, conceptually simple, and the theory is relevant to active matter, biological collectives and soft matter. Within my interests in stochastic and complex systems this is a particularly natural candidate.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek proposed the minimal numerical model, and Toner and Tu developed the continuum hydrodynamic theory with renormalisation-group results. This is a clean, plausible three-person split between model and theory, though it omits later contributors in experiment and theory (e.g. Ramaswamy, Marchetti).
assessment.maturity: The framework is widely used, but quantitative confirmation of the Toner-Tu exponents in experiment is limited and partly debated. Recognition may be somewhat early relative to the confirmation of the specific predictions.
uncertainties: Quantitative experimental confirmation of the predicted scaling exponents is incomplete, in my assessment.
Other active-matter pioneers, such as Ramaswamy, Marchetti and Cates, are not included, so credit is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the entanglement-based E91 protocol introduced provably secure key distribution based on quantum physics, and these ideas are the origin of quantum cryptography. It is original and has produced a real field and technology. I treat this ballot ID as the QKD-focused entry and prefer it to the otherwise equivalent QKD-plus-teleportation entry.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the authors of BB84 and Ekert of the entanglement-based protocol, so the three-name configuration is natural. Teleportation (also Bennett and Brassard with collaborators) is a separate discovery with additional co-authors, and I keep attention on the key-distribution contribution.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed with satellite and fibre demonstrations, but the 2022 prize on entanglement tests already recognised part of this area. Practical security issues of implementation remain, though the concept is mature.
uncertainties: Partial overlap with the 2022 Nobel Prize on Bell tests and quantum information science.
The prize here is for a theoretical-protocol idea whose practical deployment is still limited.
A duplicate candidate (QKD with teleportation) exists in the longlist, which could split the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire materials. It is a clear case of theory and experiment matching to give a surprising new platform for strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction of the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators observed the correlated and superconducting phases in 2018. This is a fair theory-experiment split. Cao and other co-authors in the 2018 experiments are not credited, which is a minor allocation concern.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have confirmed the phases, but the origin of superconductivity and many details are still under study, so the interpretation is not yet stable. Recognition is probably slightly premature, but strongly supported.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity and other correlated phases is not settled.
Sample-quality dependence and reproducibility have been issues, and I cannot independently check how fully they have been resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 confirmed the mechanism of mass generation in the Standard Model and is one of the most significant measurements in particle physics. The importance is beyond doubt, though the 2013 prize recognised the theory and not the experiment.
assessment.attribution: The 2012 result was a collaboration effort by thousands, and the Nobel rules limit the prize to three people. The names here are the proposers or spokespersons of the experiments, and the list contains four names, so any three-person choice is difficult to defend. I select two CMS leaders and one ATLAS leader as a compromise, without claiming that this is an optimal or uncontested allocation.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by two experiments and many follow-up measurements, and the interpretation as the Standard Model Higgs is stable. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue, but the allocation problem is acute.
uncertainties: A fair three-person allocation among thousands of contributors and four credited leaders is unresolved.
Choosing between leaders and other crucial physicists (e.g. detector or analysis conveners) is not supported by the supplied evidence.
The 2013 prize may be seen as having already covered the discovery.
